label: Contemporary romance
description: A love story first: chemistry, a clear external obstacle and an internal wound, alternating or single POV, and a guaranteed happy ending.
voice: First or close third person, past tense; if two POVs, alternate by chapter and label nothing, just make the voices distinct.
Emotional interiority matters, but every feeling is tied to a concrete moment.
Banter with real wit; each lead has a different sense of humour.
The obstacle is concrete (a job, a family, a lie), and so is the wound.
Heat level follows the author's directives; if none are given, fade to black.
Happily ever after (or for now) is required.

structure.guide: A meeting with sparks and friction.
A reason they must keep meeting.
structure.then: Growing attraction and resistance; one new truth per chapter.

structure.guide: The first kiss or clear crossing of a line.
They let each other in; the obstacle grows.
The wound and the obstacle break them apart.
One of them changes and proves it.
The ending that pays off the promise of the premise.

outline_guidance: Each chapter moves the relationship one visible step and shows the obstacle in action.
outline_example: Terms and Conditions | At the Larkin Bay bakery she is about to lose, Nora Kell signs Evan Shaw's fake-dating contract on the back of a flour receipt | She gets six weeks of rent; he gets a date to his ex's wedding | Evan's sister recognises Nora from the viral video
scene_guidance: Put the leads in the same room with a problem.
Let the dialogue do the work.
worldbuilding: Each lead's job, family and wound
naming: Contemporary names that fit the setting.
sample:
"Six weeks," Evan said. "Two dinners a week, one wedding, no kissing unless someone's watching."

Nora read the receipt he had written it on. Flour, 25 kg. Sugar, 10 kg. Fake boyfriend, one.

"And if someone's always watching?"

He opened his mouth, closed it, and took the pen back to add a clause.
